# Synthetic video fixture contract

No third-party videos or TeraBox shares are used. `tests/browser/run.mjs` generates a four-second 320×180, 24 fps H.264/yuv420p test pattern using FFmpeg `testsrc2`, without audio, and remuxes it to a VOD HLS playlist with one-second MPEG-TS segments. This project's synthetic fixture content is dedicated under **CC0-1.0**: https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/. The surrounding source code retains the repository's MIT license; FFmpeg/hls.js keep their own licenses. No video bytes are committed.

- Ownership/authorization: project-generated synthetic geometry; no human recording, user media, account or external CDN asset.
- Origin: `https://media.terastream.test` is an isolated test-only origin intercepted by Playwright, never a public service. Only `/clip.mp4`, `/playlist.m3u8` and `/segment-<digits>.ts` are served. Requests outside the application or fixture origin fail the test.
- CORS: allow the exact ephemeral test-app origin; GET/HEAD/OPTIONS, Range allowed, Content-Length/Content-Range/Accept-Ranges exposed. No credentialed CORS, cookies or authorization. The harness implements 206 byte ranges for native MP4 and MIME types `video/mp4`, `application/vnd.apple.mpegurl`, `video/mp2t`.
- Redirects: none. The fixture playlist references relative segments on the same fixture origin; no encryption keys, subtitles, interstitials or steering service.
- Expiry: test source assertions are issued for one minute. Unit/component cases also exercise expiry and rejection; the assertion is test data, not evidence of TeraBox authorization.
- Storage: FFmpeg writes only generated fixture bytes under a temporary directory, then the harness removes it in `finally`. Playwright fulfills browser requests directly; no application server or production route hosts/caches the media. `.dockerignore` excludes the entire test harness and fixtures.
- CSP: the isolated Vite harness uses the exact fixture media/connect origin plus `blob:` for MediaSource and `worker-src 'none'`. It replaces only the media-origin approval module during the test bundle. Production has no approved media origins and continues to use `media-src 'none'`.

The `.test` URLs used by unit tests are declarations of this synthetic contract, not working Internet endpoints. Browser decoding tests use the generated bytes. Neither class of test verifies a real TeraBox API or CDN.
